title: Authentication, Password Hashing (Argon2/bcrypt) & Access Control
summary: Distinguish Authentication vs Authorization, protect credentials cleanly with salted memory-hard hashing, and shut down IDOR vulnerabilities.
learningObjectives: Contrast fast digests (SHA-256) with salted memory-hard key derivation (Argon2id/bcrypt)
Eliminate Broken Object Level Authorization (IDOR) by scoping backend mutations strictly to session ownership
prerequisiteConcepts: HTTP sessions and backend API routes

sections.heading: 1. Credential Storage & AuthN vs AuthZ Boundaries
sections.content:
Authentication (`AuthN`) answers 'Who are you?'; Authorization (`AuthZ`) checks 'Are you allowed to access/modify THIS specific record?'. Broken Access Control / IDOR (OWASP #1!) happens when routes verify login state (`if (!userId) return 401`) yet forget verifying ownership (`AND owner_id = userId`)—letting any signed-in student read peers' grades simply by changing `?id=102`!

Meanwhile, raw passwords MUST NEVER be encrypted reversibly or hashed with fast general algorithms (MD5/SHA-256). Always use salted, memory-hard password hashes (`Argon2id` or `bcrypt`) designed specifically to throttle offline GPU cracking rigs.

codeExamples.code:
Client Request -> [1. AuthN Check: Valid Signed Session -> userId]
                      | (Fail -> HTTP 401 Unauthorized)
                      v
                  [2. AuthZ Check: record.ownerId === userId?]
                      | (Fail -> HTTP 403 / 404 Denied -> Stop IDOR!)
                      v
                  [3. Verified Domain Execution]
codeExamples.explanation: Enforcing both identity verification and resource ownership stops cross-account horizontal privilege escalation.

keyPoints: Every backend resource query must bind explicitly `.eq('owner_id', authenticatedUserId)`.
Compare secret HMACs/tokens in constant time (`timingSafeEqual`) preventing timing side-channels.
commonMistakes: Reading `userId` blindly from user-editable JSON `req.body.userId` instead of verified server auth context!

sections.heading: 2. Hardened Server AuthZ Route Pattern
sections.content: Look how concise, rock-solid authorization stays cleanly on the server: never trust submitted identity parameters (`body.ownerId`), derive `userId` strictly from the verified session token, and scope DB queries directly.

codeExamples.explanation: Pairing `.eq('id', id).eq('owner_clerk_user_id', userId)` makes horizontal IDOR impossible atomically at the DB layer.
codeExamples.expectedOutput: Cross-user deletions blocked deterministically without leaking peer record presence

keyPoints: Enforce Postgres Row-Level Security (RLS) policies mirroring API ownership checks as defense in depth.
commonMistakes: Returning different error timings or explicit `'Record belongs to admin@corp.com'` hints revealing private ownership.

exercises.title: Audit & Patch an IDOR Vulnerability
exercises.objective: Eliminate client-trusted `ownerId` and missing ownership predicates from a notes API.
exercises.description: Inspect `GET /api/notes?id=55&userId=usr_2` which returns `SELECT * FROM notes WHERE id = $1` without verifying `userId` against session context.
instructions: Retrieve authenticated `session.userId` cleanly and reject missing sessions with 401.
Scope SQL query via `WHERE id = $1 AND owner_id = $2`.
hints: Ignore any `userId` supplied in request body or query params.
exercises.submissionRequirements: Complete all checklist items, test assumptions, and document verification rationale.
evaluationCriteria: Addresses the root architectural/technical challenge accurately
Follows defensive industry standards and edge-case validation
exercises.solutionExplanation: Extracting identity solely from verified sessions and binding `AND owner_id = $2` shuts down IDOR cleanly.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Why does trusting `req.body.userId` instead of verified session `auth().userId` create an immediate vulnerability?

options.text: Any attacker can forge any victim's `userId` inside JSON bodies and impersonate accounts freely
JSON bodies cannot parse UUID strings
It triggers syntax errors in TypeScript

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Authenticated subject identity must come strictly from verified server session tokens/cookies.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Why is Argon2id strictly recommended over raw SHA-256 for storing user password digests?

options.text: Argon2id consumes configurable memory and CPU work factor with unique salts, making GPU brute-force cracking orders of magnitude slower
SHA-256 outputs can be decoded straight back to strings via algebra
Argon2id removes the need for HTTPS
SHA-256 only hashes passwords shorter than 8 characters

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Fast hashes fail against GPU cracking farms; slow memory-hard functions defend user credentials cleanly.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: What vulnerability allows Student A to view Student B's exam submission simply by requesting `/api/attempts/1002` instead of `1001`?
knowledgeChecks.explanation: Failing to enforce ownership per requested resource ID causes IDOR / BOLA.

recap: You reinforced AuthN vs AuthZ separation, password KDF selection, and atomic IDOR prevention.
